content.thinking:
I'm planning the capybara's proportions and pose, sketching out realistic body dimensions and positioning along the z-axis for the barrel-shaped torso, with a bird perched on its head.

Now I'm working out the skeleton structure—hips as root joint, with a spine chain running through multiple segments up to the neck and head, placing joints at specific coordinates to curve naturally from the lower back through the shoulders into a long blunt snout typical of a capybara's head shape.

I'm adding a small tail stub joint at the rump, then setting up the limb system: front legs angled with knees bending backward like a capybara's elbow, hind legs bending forward, calculating segment lengths to ensure the IK reach matches the distance from hip/shoulder height down to the ground.

For feet, I'm placing toes at the tip joint of each limb chain -- four toes on the front feet and three on the hind feet, using small capsule or sphere shapes to represent them, parented correctly through the spine or hip joints depending on whether they're front or back legs.

For the body, I'm sweeping a loft path from the rump through the spine to the neck, binding it to the hips, spine, and neck joints so it deforms correctly as the chain animates.

Setting up colors with a cel-shaded toon look over fur edges—orange coat with a lighter tan belly, dark shadow tones, and a mottled texture variation blended into the base coat color for natural variegation.

Now building the head: a skull sphere scaled into an ellipsoid shape attached at a forward-leaning head joint, plus a separate smaller sphere for the blunt snout positioned just below it.

Adding the nose pad as a dark sphere at the front with tiny dark nostril spheres, a lower jaw sphere scaled in cream and parented to its own jaw joint aiming slightly upward, small rounded ears with dark pink inner spheres set on the back of the head, and dark eye spheres with white highlight dots placed high on the head to match capybara proportions.

Checking that the eye position stays clear of the snout sphere overlap, it looks fine given the geometry. For whiskers, I'll add thin rod primitives extending from the muzzle outward on both sides, four per side in a tan-ish color.

For fur, I'm planning to scatter small light-grey svg tuft cards across the body surface, around 500 of them, relying on the part's color paint to tint them to the coat color -- that keeps the triangle count manageable at roughly 2000 total.

I'll split the scatter between body (450 cards) and head (120 cards) using each part's own surface, filtering out cards on the underside with a height threshold so fur only grows where it should, and letting bone weights drive bend. For the legs, I'm sweeping tapered tubes with a radius function that narrows toward the foot, and shading them with a gradient from the coat color into a darker brown near the paws.

I need to watch the foot placement carefully since the round end cap on the sweep extends past the last point by its radius -- so I'm setting the foot's target height and tapering the end radius to keep the paw just above the ground rather than clipping through it, then working out leg segment lengths to match.

For toes I'm using small scaled spheres that sit just above the floor, checking the scaled radius doesn't dip below zero. For the hip joints, I'm placing the leg root points relative to the body, adding a small tail stub sphere at the hips, and sketching out a separate joint hierarchy for the bird perched on the head -- root, head, wings, tail, beak -- keeping it simple while still rigged.

Now I'm defining the bird body joint attached near the head, considering tilting its facing direction slightly off-axis so it reads as a 3/4 turn, and sketching the bird's body as a small scaled sphere with blue-tit coloring (blue back, yellow belly, white cheek, blue cap, black eye stripe) using a countershaded, cel-shaded paint style.

Continuing with the head sphere, I'm planning its coloring with a countershade between blue and white for the cheeks, adding small black eye spheres, and a thin dark rod stroke suggesting the eye stripe, then starting on the beak as a small spike protruding from the head.

Now I'm working out the wings as scaled, rotated spheres positioned on either side with blue coloring and striped wing bars for texture, and beginning to plan the tail using a tapered frustum shape.

Dark toes as tiny spheres, with the bird body bottom around y=0.70, so I'll run its legs from 0.705 to 0.668. For the skeleton, I need unique joint names for the bird parts and need to make sure hips is created first as the root. The neck chain should connect to the end of the spine chain at the same point, so I'm checking how chain parenting works to pass the right parent joint.

Spine chain parents off hips, starting at hips' position and running through three segments named spine1-3 with role "spine". Then neck runs two more segments named neck1-2 with role "neck", and the head joint attaches at the neck's endpoint, parented to neck.joints[1].

For the loft stations, I'm checking height proportions — placing a small station near the rear at roughly 0.36 height and widening into the torso at 0.37, but I'm noticing the math pushes the body top to around 0.62, which might clash with the head sphere positioned at 0.68, so I need to double check belly clearance and overall height isn't stacking the head above the torso incorrectly.

Adding the remaining tail stations to narrow the rump down, then checking the hip joint alignment near z -0.4. For the head I'm adding cheek and jaw spheres, and thinking through a thin curved mouth line swept along the snout's front surface, positioning the snout center and radii to match.

Still computing facial geometry... I'm adjusting the mouth line curve, nose pad sphere position, and nostril placements to avoid overlap with the jaw and snout shapes.

Checking the color palette count stays under the limit, then assigning coat paint variants for the skull, snout, and underside cream areas, plus a darker muzzle tone. For the eyes, I'm placing a small white highlight sphere offset from the main eye position to suggest light reflection.

Now I'm working out ear placement by checking the skull sphere's curvature at that x-position to make sure the ear sits properly against the head surface, along with adding an inner darker pink layer for depth.

Adjusting ear orientation to flat sideways-facing ovals with inner ear offset, then working out toe placement around the feet—4 toes for front, 3 for hind, spaced along the foot tip.

I'm adding a broader foot pad sphere under the leg, flattened and scaled so its lowest point sits right at ground level, then setting up a gradient from coat color to a darker leg shade. For the foot joints, I need to find the right way to reference the last joint in the chain since the tip might not have the expected type.

Now I'm working out hind and front leg placement for the capybara - hip roots, foot positions, and bend directions to make the knees angle correctly, plus adding extra haunch spheres around the hip joints for visual thickness.

Skipping the haunch idea since the body is wide enough already; instead I'm tapering the leg radius from thick at the hip to thin at the foot, using a radius array along the sweep chain. Then I'm adding a small tail nub sphere attached to a tail joint bone.

For fur, I'm designing a tuft texture as an SVG path shaped like a teardrop, rendering it at a modest canvas size with the root anchored at the bottom edge of the drawing so it can be tiled upward along the body.

Now I'm checking the scatter setup for fur cards across the body surface — using a seeded RNG, a minimum spacing of about 0.035 across roughly 1.5 square meters of area, and a default lean/flow angle for the cards. Then I'm defining a rod primitive for the whiskers bound to the head with configurable radius and color, and confirming cheek tufts follow the same pattern.

Adding jaw and teeth details, then double-checking imports for unused modules...

Now I'm setting up the bird's wing joints, naming them by side, and placing ellipsoid wing shapes with minimal rotation tweaks.

I'm positioning the bird's body, head, eye, beak, and tail using layered ellipsoids and frustum shapes, carefully overlapping them for natural proportions.

Now I'm wiring up the bird's skeleton joints, setting parent-child relationships for the tail and legs bones, then moving on to coloring the body with a countershaded cel-shading pattern and the wings with a striped pattern.

Checking a few remaining details: the head countershading, a sphere helper for rounded parts, and side-naming conventions for left/right joints. Then adding surface scatter detail on the skull for texture.

Working out the mouth sweep shape with its rounded caps, and setting up the head joint's position and direction relative to the neck, with the jaw as its own role. That should be everything needed to finalize the code.
